claims.title: Lucayan settlement of the islands
claims.summary: The Lucayans, a Taíno (Arawakan) people, migrated from Hispaniola and Cuba and settled the Bahamian archipelago, eventually numbering perhaps 40,000 across dozens of islands.

claims.title: Columbus's first landfall at Guanahani
claims.summary: Christopher Columbus made his first landfall in the Americas at the Lucayan island of Guanahani, which he renamed San Salvador and claimed for Castile, opening the European encounter with the New World.

claims.title: Spanish enslavement of the Lucayans
claims.summary: Spanish raiders began systematically seizing Lucayans as forced labour for the mines and pearl fisheries of the Greater Antilles and Venezuela, devastating the islands' population.

claims.title: Depopulation of the Bahamas
claims.summary: By about 1520 enslavement and disease had all but exterminated the Lucayans; the islands were left effectively abandoned for more than a century.

claims.title: The Eleutheran Adventurers settle Eleuthera
claims.summary: English Puritans led by William Sayle left Bermuda seeking religious freedom and founded the first lasting English settlement in the Bahamas on the island they named Eleuthera ("freedom").

claims.title: Grant to the Lords Proprietors of Carolina
claims.summary: The Bahamas were granted to the Lords Proprietors of Carolina, though their rule proved weak and largely nominal, leaving the scattered islands poorly governed.

claims.title: Nassau becomes a pirate haven
claims.summary: Amid a collapse of royal authority, Nassau became the base of a loose pirate republic, home to Blackbeard, Charles Vane, Anne Bonny and others who preyed on Atlantic shipping.

claims.title: Woodes Rogers ends the pirate republic
claims.summary: Royal governor Woodes Rogers arrived at Nassau with the King's Pardon, accepted the surrender of many pirates, drove out the rest and restored Crown authority under the motto "Pirates Expelled, Commerce Restored".

claims.title: Spain cedes the Bahamas to Britain
claims.summary: Under the Treaty of Paris of 1783 Spain ceded the Bahamas to Britain, securing the colony's future under the Crown after years of contest and a brief Spanish occupation.

claims.title: American Loyalists and enslaved Africans arrive
claims.summary: Loyalist refugees from the new United States emigrated to the Bahamas after the American Revolution, bringing thousands of enslaved Africans and roughly trebling the colony's population.

claims.title: The failed cotton plantations
claims.summary: Loyalists planted cotton on the "Cotton Islands", but exhausted soils and pests ruined the crop within a couple of decades, collapsing the plantation economy.

claims.title: Slavery Abolition Act takes effect
claims.summary: The British Slavery Abolition Act came into force in the Bahamas on 1 August 1834, beginning emancipation; after an apprenticeship period, full freedom followed in 1838.

claims.title: An economy of wrecking and sponging
claims.summary: The poor post-emancipation colony lived largely on salvaging shipwrecks, sponge-fishing and salt, with wrecking for a time its single largest source of income.

claims.title: Civil War blockade-running boom
claims.summary: During the American Civil War, Nassau became the chief hub for running the Union blockade, shipping arms to the Confederacy and cotton out, and growing fabulously wealthy in the process.

claims.title: Collapse of the blockade boom
claims.summary: The defeat of the Confederacy in 1865 ended blockade-running overnight and plunged Nassau back into economic depression.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Bahamas: From the Lucayan islanders and Columbus's first New World landfall, through Spanish depopulation, the pirate republic of Nassau, Loyalist plantations and emancipation, to majority rule, independence in 1973, and a modern nation of tourism, finance and hurricanes.", terralore.co/country/BHS/chronicle#ev-1865-collapse-of-the-blockade-boom, claim TL:BHS:event:1865:collapse-of-the-blockade-boom, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Prohibition-era rum-running
claims.summary: American Prohibition turned the Bahamas into a base for smuggling liquor across the Gulf Stream, enriching the colony until repeal in 1933 ended the trade.

claims.title: Founding of the Progressive Liberal Party
claims.summary: Bahamians opposed to UBP and "Bay Street" dominance founded the Progressive Liberal Party, which became the vehicle of the movement for majority rule.

claims.title: Internal self-government
claims.summary: A new constitution granted the Bahamas internal self-government with a cabinet and a first premier, while Britain retained defence and external affairs.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Bahamas: From the Lucayan islanders and Columbus's first New World landfall, through Spanish depopulation, the pirate republic of Nassau, Loyalist plantations and emancipation, to majority rule, independence in 1973, and a modern nation of tourism, finance and hurricanes.", terralore.co/country/BHS/chronicle#ev-1964-internal-self-government, claim TL:BHS:event:1964:internal-self-government, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Majority rule — the Quiet Revolution
claims.summary: Lynden Pindling's PLP gained power after the 1967 election, making him the first Black premier and ending the long political dominance of the white "Bay Street" elite.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Bahamas: From the Lucayan islanders and Columbus's first New World landfall, through Spanish depopulation, the pirate republic of Nassau, Loyalist plantations and emancipation, to majority rule, independence in 1973, and a modern nation of tourism, finance and hurricanes.", terralore.co/country/BHS/chronicle#ev-1967-majority-rule-the-quiet-revolution, claim TL:BHS:event:1967:majority-rule-the-quiet-revolution, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Independence of The Bahamas
claims.summary: The Commonwealth of The Bahamas became independent of the United Kingdom on 10 July 1973 under Prime Minister Lynden Pindling, remaining a Commonwealth realm and joining the United Nations.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Bahamas: From the Lucayan islanders and Columbus's first New World landfall, through Spanish depopulation, the pirate republic of Nassau, Loyalist plantations and emancipation, to majority rule, independence in 1973, and a modern nation of tourism, finance and hurricanes.", terralore.co/country/BHS/chronicle#ev-1973-independence-of-the-bahamas, claim TL:BHS:event:1973:independence-of-the-bahamas, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: First peaceful change of government
claims.summary: Hubert Ingraham's Free National Movement defeated the PLP in 1992, ending Lynden Pindling's twenty-five years in power in the country's first democratic alternation of government.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Bahamas: From the Lucayan islanders and Columbus's first New World landfall, through Spanish depopulation, the pirate republic of Nassau, Loyalist plantations and emancipation, to majority rule, independence in 1973, and a modern nation of tourism, finance and hurricanes.", terralore.co/country/BHS/chronicle#ev-1992-first-peaceful-change-of-government, claim TL:BHS:event:1992:first-peaceful-change-of-government, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Hurricane Dorian devastates Abaco and Grand Bahama
claims.summary: Category 5 Hurricane Dorian stalled over the northern Bahamas, killing scores, leaving hundreds missing and causing about US$3.4 billion in damage — roughly a quarter of GDP.
